items.followUp: Why does atomic radius decrease from left to right across a period?

rubric.why: An additional occupied shell is added as we move down a group.
rubric.description: States that the number of occupied electron shells increases down a group.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the increase in occupied electron shells.

rubric.why: The increased distance of the outer electrons from the nucleus leads to a larger atom.
rubric.description: Explains that the outermost electrons are farther from the nucleus, so atomic size increases.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the increased distance or resulting increase in atomic size or radius.

modelAnswer: The number of occupied electron shells increases down a group.
The outermost electrons are farther from the nucleus, so the atomic size increases.

items.followUp: Define a covalent bond and give one example of a molecule containing it.

rubric.why: Sharing electron pairs is the defining feature of a covalent bond.
rubric.description: Defines a covalent bond as one formed by sharing one or more pairs of electrons between atoms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that atoms share electron pairs.

rubric.why: A valid example demonstrates a covalent bond.
rubric.description: Gives one valid example of a covalent substance.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example, such as H₂.

modelAnswer: A covalent bond is formed when atoms share one or more pairs of electrons.
For example, the bond between the two atoms in H₂ is covalent.

items.followUp: Using electronegativity difference, classify a bond with a difference of 2.1 as ionic or covalent.

rubric.why: Bond type is classified by comparing the electronegativities of the bonded atoms.
rubric.description: States that the difference between the atoms’ electronegativities is used.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying electronegativity difference as the basis of classification.

rubric.why: The stated threshold and classifications distinguish ionic from covalent bonds.
rubric.description: States the rule: a difference greater than 1.7 indicates an ionic bond, while a difference less than 1.7 indicates a covalent bond.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving the 1.7 threshold and the corresponding bond types.

modelAnswer: Find the difference between the electronegativities of the two bonded atoms.
If the difference is greater than 1.7, the bond is ionic; if it is less than 1.7, the bond is covalent.
